Title: Overview of MediaEval 2020 Predicting Media Memorability Task: What Makes a Video Memorable?

Abstract: This paper describes the MediaEval 2020 \textit{Predicting Media Memorability} task. After first being proposed at MediaEval 2018, the Predicting Media Memorability task is in its 3rd edition this year, as the prediction of short-term and long-term video memorability (VM) remains a challenging task. In 2020, the format remained the same as in previous editions. This year the videos are a subset of the TRECVid 2019 Video-to-Text dataset, containing more action rich video content as compared with the 2019 task. Title: Investigating Memorability of Dynamic Media

Abstract: The Predicting Media Memorability task in MediaEval'20 has some challenging aspects compared to previous years. In this paper we identify the high-dynamic content in videos and dataset of limited size as the core challenges for the task, we propose directions to overcome some of these challenges and we present our initial result in these directions.
input_records.title: Investigating Memorability of Dynamic Media

input_records.abstract: Memorability determines what evanesces into emptiness, and what worms its way into the deepest furrows of our minds. It is the key to curating more meaningful media content as we wade through daily digital torrents. The Predicting Media Memorability task in MediaEval 2020 aims to address the question of media memorability by setting the task of automatically predicting video memorability. Our approach is a multimodal deep learning-based late fusion that combines visual, semantic, and auditory features. We used audio gestalt to estimate the influence of the audio modality on overall video memorability, and accordingly inform which combination of features would best predict a given video's memorability scores.

Abstract: Memorability determines what evanesces into emptiness, and what worms its way into the deepest furrows of our minds. It is the key to curating more meaningful media content as we wade through daily digital torrents. The Predicting Media Memorability task in MediaEval 2020 aims to address the question of media memorability by setting the task of automatically predicting video memorability. **Research Question:**  
How can the integration of audio gestalt features with visual and semantic cues improve the prediction of short-term video memorability compared to using visual and semantic features alone?

**Rationale:**  
This question is specific, novel, and answerable based on the provided research papers. It builds on the existing work in the Predicting Media Memorability task by focusing on the contribution of audio gestalt—a concept not previously emphasized in the earlier editions of the task. The question invites an investigation into whether the inclusion of audio-based features, particularly those capturing the "gestalt" or holistic perception of sound, enhances the accuracy of memorability prediction. It also aligns with the challenges mentioned in the papers, such as the high-dynamic content and limited dataset size, by suggesting that multimodal approaches may offer more robust predictions.
